"Grocery store grade" ice creams beat you over the head with sweetness and flavorings. Even some premium brands are rather intense. THIS is the place to go if you want a true flavor experience. After savoring pints of the Rising Star coffee and salted caramel, the thing that stands out most is the subtlety. This is a premium product that caresses the taste buds with enticing, subtle hints of the featured ingredients on top of a solid base that is not cloyingly sweet. Not cheap, but the ice cream equivalent of a meal prepared by a master chef.
Best Ice cream In town... bing cherry chocolate chip, key lime pie are just phenomenal. Been coming around for years and have yet to find a reason not to keep coming back

Bouchon, I finally found you. I've been to Vegas how many times and I always seem to miss your macarons. I made it a point to find you this past trip. You offer expensive baked goods but the macaron variety pack is well worth the trip to the Venetian. I paid $17.50 for 6 macarons (lemon, orange, strawberry, chocolate, coffee, and vanilla). My favorite was the lemon one - very refreshing. These macarons are huge - bigger than most macarons I've seen from other places. Unfortunately they didn't travel well. These are delicate cookies that almost didn't survive the heat and the flight. But I got them home and the edges were crumbly and the creamy filling had partially melted. But still, they tasted good. The case with the baked goods looked tempting - I would have gotten one of each if I had the space in my suitcase.

was just there over Valentine's Day weekend....and HORRIBLE service! My hubby only ordered 1-scoop of ice cream in a cup.....and stood there with only 2 people ahead of us waiting for their order and only 1 person, at a turtle-pace making the orders....while 4 other workers stood around chatting.....cashier, supervisor/manager and 2 others. As we asked about our 1 small scoop of ice cream....the supervisor/manager stated that she (the only worker slowly doing the orders) were completing the orders in order of coming in - well, then why the heck aren't you back there helping her as you see several customers standing there waiting! Never going back!

Love this place!! When we're in the area we try to stop by the store. On one occasion my son's ice cream fell off his cone as soon as he licked it and it was one of those scenes from a comic strips where the child has an empty cone in hand and the single scoop is on the floor. Even though I offered to clean up the ice cream on the floor and pay for another scoop of ice cream, the employees were nice enough to give us a free scoop and told me they would clean it up. Great customer service and unique flavors that you can't find anywhere else!

Okay I get it it's a place from tv.... But to be honest this place isn't that amazing. First off the lady who took my order shorted me on not one but two things! And it took her 5x's as long as any other person to pack it. They need someone too double check the orders before they send it out! I mean come on they pretty much stole 10$ from us.
Everything I have gotten from here is very good, and the staff is super friendly!!! Love recommending this place to people.

Love this place. We tried tons of sweets, but our favorites were salted caramel brownie, pecan tart and lemon raspberry tart. Skip the twice baked almond croissant and the regular croissants. Even though the salted caramel macaron previously was my favorite thing I'd ever eaten, this time there was no salt flavor so it was a little boring. The latte of the day (I think it was St. Laurent Spice) was amazing.
Omg the donut bar is so great if you haven't tried it suggest you do so. sooooooooo yummy

OMG!! So yummy! Make sure you get there early!! The donuts are huge!! I got the grill cheese one the last time I went and it was so amazing. Along with the staff always upbeat and happy. And so many vegan options as well.

I'm totally not a cupcake person except for Sprinkles. Doesn't matter where it is, whether it'd be LA, NYC or Vegas, they're all consistent and taste yummy every time! Moist cupcakes, excellent cake to frosting ratio, awesome flavours!!!

OH MY YUMMY I have a strong appreciation for many things in life and one of them is cupcakes. Sprinkles needs to expand west and get some more locations near me! Or maybe it's best they stay in Vegas so I have an excuse to go back! There is such a great variety here. All of their ingredients are pronounceable it almost makes me want to endorse the place as healthy! This is only my second visit and I "only" got two this time but they were both wonderful. I ate them too fast I forgot to take pictures (no, not both at the same time)! I ordered the triple cinnamon or double something or other, it tasted like a snickerdoodle spice cake with cinnamon frosting. The second was the "sprinkles" flavor which I believe is just their vanilla cake with white frosting and rainbow sprinkles. Both hit the spot. The place is always packed it seems, but the servers stay happy and always seem to be smiling. It's open late and there is an ice cream bar attached that is also quite tasty! A place I will definitely make a point to visit every time I come to Vegas.

I am originally from Akron, so thought we had the only beloved Mary Coyle's on earth. Imagine my surprise when I moved to Phoenix and discovered the sister store and a place beloved just as much here. My grandmother took me to Mary Coyle's as a child and it was always a special outing. As an older adult, I still return to my childhood favorites--a root-beer float or hot fudge sundae with whipped cream. This is my favorite ice cream place in the Valley of the Sun or if in Akron at Highland Square. What a lucky girl to have had them both!

I tried Dripps for a second time today and I was really impressed by the drink I got. The owner recommended a matcha coffee (I'm usually not a fan of matcha or coffee) and it was surprisingly so good. I'll never drink coffee straight but I took a sip of the coffee before I stirred the drink and I could probably have a whole glass of that cold brew. Considering I was the only order, I think it did take some time. They seemed to crush the matcha powder (or something time consuming) fresh and put it in which is nice to see it be fresh but it took a few minutes for a simple matcha coffee being the only order there. I will be back for another. Thanks

Disappointed dry cheese cake Walmart has better deals plus it was 13 bucks I can't believe it after watching the show thought this place would be amazing I guess they just going for looks not taste don't eat here not worth it

After a late morning at MOCA, we headed to Little Italy and Presti's. This is a great lunch spot for people with diverse tastes as there is everything from pizza, to pastas,salads and panininis. All reasonably priced, with a great selection from their bakery for desert. (Hint: save room for Creme Brulee). It can get a bit crowded at lunch and be sure to take a number as they use them, and won't get around to you as fast if you just stand in line. Yes, it's a bit confusing, but that's part of the fun. They bring the food to your table and you bus your plates once you have finished.
Amazing ice cream, awesome owners, not to be missed! Unique flavors all made small batch, like nothing you will find other places

Being a first time customer I wanted to try a few pints and see what grabbed me. I should have gotten the sampler plate. I would have gotten the taste of all 4 for a better bang for my buck. The gram central station - I liked it a lot, if you're a fan of the gram, it's for you. Chocolate peanut butter was good. 90% dark chocolate. We got a couple others that were tasty, not sure I'd drive to the other part of town for them again. But if I'm in the neighborhood it's a good stop.

Not impressed. The crack pie and cornflake chocolate chip marshmallow cookie tasted fake. The fruit cereal ice cream was probably the better out of the three items we tried. Everything was outrageously overpriced for what it is.
Best Ice cream in the city! Gooey butter cake is amazing and the handmade waffle cones put it all together.

The edible cookie dough is HORRIBLE. I didn't read the ingredients first, took a bite, and thought it tasted just like butter. THEN I read the ingredients and it's basically just butter and shortening. I took one bite each of two flavors, then my wife did the same, and we literally threw three tubs into the trash.
First time trying this place just walking by. It's good but I would say it's a little pricey. I would stil try it just to taste and know.

Was super excited to try out Milk Bar after watching Christina Tosi's episode of Chef's Table and knew I had to stop by. We ordered a slice of crack pie and a cereal milk soft serve as a post-lunch dessert. As many others have said, everything here is expensive and in my opinion, not worth the high price-tag. The cereal milk soft serve tasted nice, wasn't too sweet, and had a lighter texture than many soft serves I've tried before but I felt that there really wasn't anything special or memorable about it- at least not enough to warrant $6 (& this is without the cereal flakes on top). Now moving on to the crack pie, I was pretty shocked with the size, this thing is SMALL. My boyfriend is honestly still appalled that we paid over $6 for this but I personally think it's a better deal than the soft serve. Yes it's small but it is really dense and filling. It has a beautiful buttery and sugary taste that I really enjoyed - I'd probably bump my rating up to 4 stars if the price of this dropped to about $4 or $5 to be honest. Overall I think Milk Bar is the type of place you visit just to say you've visited. The prices are simply too high- even if it does taste pretty good. I would only be back if I was SUPER craving crack pie or if I won a nice little jackpot downstairs (then I'd buy the entire crack pie for ~$50)
Sometimes the line is crazy long, and sometimes just the wait to get your sandwich is really long. food is worth it though. and its awesome that it's 4 hours. but there is usually always a long wait.
Shop faces Carson not 6th. We walked from Fremont took a few extra steps, but well worth it.

It's a little on the pricy side for ice cream, but worth every penny. The ice cream is delicious, and options well varied, the staff friendly, everything clean. This place is bomb. If they have pumpkin spice...GET IT. the salted Carmel is made in house as is the phenomenal toffee. Worth the drive and expense.

I don't eat a lot of ice cream, when I do fresh McConnell's is my favorite. what is perfect ice cream? The perfect balance between sweetness, creaminess and texture is different for everyone so there is no right or wrong answer. This hits the spot for me and I don't have to go to California to get it. So good I ate all 4 flavours in the sampler by my self! I tried blueberry cobbler which didn't taste like a cobbler, just blueberry. Coffee chocolate chip, which was my favorite, tasted like a late rather than boring drip coffee. Spouse like a house (I know right) this one is a little more elaborate with peanut butter cups, peanut butter ripple and chocolate covered peanut butter filled pretzels. The pretzels are chocolate covered so they, maintain their crunch unlike others that get soggy or stale. Caramel pretzel had the same chocolate covered peanut butter filled pretzels with a Carmel ribbon. Subtle and perfect. Bring on the food coma!
Wonderful craft ice cream in grant arts area. Worth finding. The doughnut sandwich is crazy good!

Amazing ice cream! It's creamy and delicious, and there's a huge selection of flavors. I was just visiting Madison for the weekend, but I heard this place is a chain, so I hope to be back in the near future!

This place is spotless clean and they have all kind of flavors, interactive toys for lil kids, snow cones and a lot of treats ., We love that they create different flavors also the lady was very nice with us she even let us get an advantage to try a new flavor they are creating (red velvet/cookie monster) that was so nice of her . Also they give you samples so you can try before buying the whole scoop
So fresh, ... So good! I was not a fan of the bacon bar. It was not good and not worth the $4 price tag.

This ice cream place is covered in fun and colorful decorations filled with ice cream, candies, and toys. Unfortunately the customer service was extremely slow and there was a long line that we ended up leaving. My brother in law decided to go back 30 minutes later because it was finally empty but when we got the cookies and cream it was disappointing and underwhelming.

Feels and tastes like neighborhood ice cream shop that I remember growing up. Large selection, up beat employees, reasonable prices. Can also take pint or quart to go. Thankful that they opened so close to our home.
Great ice cream and lots of gluten free options! A little pricey but such a nice treat. Super cute store too!!

I heard this was one of the best ice cream places in Madison, and it did not disappoint! I ordered the Munchie Madness ice cream in a waffle cone, and it was amazing. The prices were a tad high, but it was still worth every penny. The place was very busy on a Saturday night, and I can see why. The inside of the restaurant was very neat as well. Lots of bright colors! I would definitely go here again!

Absolutely a wonderful experience! The staff especially Luis and Lydia where so sweet and on their job! They let you try their different flavors of ice cream, and are not pushy or hurrying you at all!!! We got an ice cream sandwich that was out of this world! The butter pecan ice cream is amazing! If you have not been you have to go! Be prepared it is a bit of a wait! But it is soooo worth it!!

Honey hut has good ice cream, but don't expect to get any other option besides ice cream. They don't serve yogurt, low sugar, sugar free, or vegan options. I emailed the company a couple of times to ask whether or not their ice cream was gluten free and what their kitchen/serving practices are and never heard back. I do know that you can ask the server for a clean scoop but as all of their ice cream is hard packed, everyone else's scoop has already been in the container. Unfortunately this is one of those places that has great ice cream, but limited/no options for those who need something a little different. That being said, if you don't have any food allergies and want some good old fashioned hard scoop ice cream, give Honey Hut a try. Their honey pecan and chocolate peanut butter are excellent options.

Around the chandler area this evening and saw this on yelp. Saw that they had matcha and I LOVE matcha from back in Cali. The matcha coffee was perfect after a big meal. Please open one out in the west valley! We need more stuff like this!!
My cupcake was good but it it didn't live up to the expectation of a cupcake from a judge on cupcake wars. I got the red velvet it wasn't bad at all, it just wasn't special.

I've ordered the vegan caramel popcorn at the melt the last 3 times I've been. The first time the popcorn was so chewy It got all stuck in my teeth... and so hard to chew.. I considered maybe it was just a bad bag.. So I gave it another chance, and ordered it a second time (because the melt doesn't have any other vegan desserts) and it was delicious! Exactly what you would expect for caramel popcorn.. sweet caramel glaze.. crunchy! Ordered it a third time, and another disappointment I don't want to blame the company.. maybe it's the way the melt stores it  but 1/3, not good odds. I did mention this to the melt, they shrugged.. Still not sure if it's supposed to be chewy.. Also, it was from different locations.. bummer..
So let me start off by saying i use to go for the cannoli every once in a while just because it tasted so different then what we were use to. For some reason they lost their great taste.

Good egg sandwiches although expensive. Good counter service. Salted caramel brownie was old, stale, took a bite then had to throw out, dry too. Next time I'd try something else but I'd recommend trying this first before you walk away, I should've returned it. That one got past quality control.

Friendly staff and great location. This is a can't miss! The oatmeal cookie dough and red velvet ice creams were sinfully delicious. I opted for the Hula Hula. Once they gave me instructions on how to properly eat it, I must say best thing I've had all day.

The girls working the counter were really friendly and helpful. But management seriously needs to add more employees to the peak hour shifts. There was one girl working the register and only one other girl serving the orders. I came on a Saturday evening and I literally waited 30 minutes for an overpriced ice cream sundae because the line was so long. It felt like I was waiting for over an hour because the girls standing in front of me in line had the worst BO that I've ever encountered. The location is great and is adjacent to many other eateries and bars by the Linq hotel. While the shop itself is relatively small, there are several tables right outside for customers to sit and eat, which is convenient. If it weren't for the wait time, I would've given the place 3 stars.
The French Toast donut is made to order so it comes out warm and comes with jelly and syrup on the side. The inside is a little small but they have lots of seating in the back.
Pretty cool place to try. I tried a few of the different fillings in the Taiyaki. Custard was yummy.

The first time ever going there it was pretty awesome. It's a pretty cool They had a lot of donuts to pick from. The donut I got was called "The Homer", yes like Homer Simpson. Classic donut, pink frosting, and sprinkles. That donut was literally bigger than my face, it was very sweet, and delicious. Totally grab a coffee or milk to go with it! Donut Bar is pretty popular. So the biggest downside is that there's not that many seats inside, they do have a few seat outside in the shade. It's Las Vegas, even in the shade it's like 102° outside. I would totally recommend someone to go to the Donut Bar in Downtown Las Vegas!

If you are looking for good ole fashion ice cream, this is the place. Sure, you can fancy it up with toppings or make it a sunday but there is really no need. The ice cream flavors and texture is great on its own! And totally reasonable for a scoop or two. I'm not gonna lie though, the toasted fluff is amazing! The parking is terrible and the line is usually out the door but grab a dose of patience, hunt down a parking spot and grab your spot in line, you won't be disappointed.

While in Vegas, we decided to embark on a macaron taste test. Bouchon was one of our contenders. Tried the Strawberry and Chocolate flavors. I don't want to spoil the other reviews but hands down, Bouchon has the best macarons ever! They were the right size - just enough to make you fall in love and want more without going overboard. Light and flaky with a sweet filling. As much as I love chocolate, my favorite here is the Strawberry!

The sweetest, most charming, little indulgent shop I know. If you're in downtown Phoenix and are craving something sweet, then you must, and I mean must, head on over to Churn. It's located on Central ave right next to Windsor (another must try btw). It features freshly made churned ice cream with simple ingredients and no added preservatives or stabilizers! This is the real, good, old school way to eat ice cream ya'll. They offer so many fun flavors and with their choices of sundaes, ice cream cookie sandwiches, milkshakes, and floats, the possibilities are endless. If ice cream isn't your thing, or you just want something sweet, their selection of candies are sure to satisfy and take you back a few years into your childhood. They also make fresh baked goods, have delicious coffee, and sell fun throwback toys like army men and yo yo's! Churn brought an instant smile to my face the moment I walked in. I couldn't help but want to try it all and the service was incredible too. What a great place to spend a beautiful spring day in Phoenix. Definitely check it out and bring the whole family for a treat they'll never forget.
Great ice cream and service! We really enjoyed coming here during our visit to Scottsdale. We will definitely be coming back.

Experienced this with my bro and his GF. We got quite a few things to sample, and nothing was as good as what you can get at the authentic french bakery in Spring Valley called BonJour Bakery. Lots of customers are chatting in French and the baked goods are phenomenal. Can't say the same of Bouchon's. Sorry - I had higher expectations of Bouch. Luckily, BonJour fulfills those expectations.

My favorite ice cream shop. They have such unique flavors that are rich and extremely tasty. First time I came I had the Cocoa Puffs and fruity pebbles.. I love the cereals and the ice cream had the same exact taste but in rich creamy ice cream form. The second time I had the flavors of my two favorite snacks: peanut butter and jelly and chocolate cake batter. The ice cream once again tasted like the exact food but in an ice cream rich consistency. I am very impressed by this place. There is always a line when I come and always people dining in on the patio in the front.

OMG! I can't believe I forgot to write this review. Novel Ice Cream has completely changed the dessert game. Thanks to the collab that Yelp did with Buzzfeed last month, I stumbled across this hot new business. I came in with two of my closest friends, and let's just say we were NOT disappointed. We waited quite awhile before it was our turn to order. Since their location is quite small, we had to wait outside. Though we weren't mad in the slightest! I mean what do you expect, it is THE best ice cream sandwich in the state of Arizona - the hype is real, people! The business owner felt bad for our long wait time, and graciously thanked us for our patience. He did everything right. He gave us suggestions, he was patient, kind, and gave us our fair turn in line. I truly wish this man the best of success! I ended up ordering the toasted almond ice cream smashed between two waffle pieces. This wouldn't typically be my go-to choice but.... WOW! It was AMAZING in every way. My two friends were completely satisfied with what they ordered, as well! I'm not a doughnut person at all, but after trying theirs my opinion changed. I hope I've talked this place up enough for you to give it a try. Believe me when I say it was well worth every calorie, and one of the most satisfying desserts I've ever had. Thank you, Novel. I will be back again, and again, and again!

So disappointing!!! Love Cake Boss and was excited to try some pastries. We tried a few different items. The seven layer cookie (I know them as rainbow cookies in NY) was very average. Tried a pecan snowball cookie. So dry!!!! And so bland. Hubs and I each got beautiful sugar cookies with sprinkles. They looked great! Once again, bland!!! Zero flavor. With so many options in Vegas, you are better off going elsewhere for sweets. The only good thing...their prices are not bad, especially for Vegas!

Not worth the hype unless your getting something Made to order like the milk ice cream. The cookies and milk bar are pre made and packaged. For the price you would expect a warm cookie and something tasting freshly made instead your getting a cold cookie and milk bar slice. Disappointed especially for price.

Not worthy at all! I waited more than 30 minutes in line, the service is veeeery bad, the whole crew doesn't know how to treat their customers. The crÃªpe is good and not that expensive but the trade-off wasn't good to me!

We have always wanted to try Sprinkles but never had the chance. Before our trip to Vegas, hubby had a huge craving for cupcakes and I saw that there was a sprinkles there. One of the days during our trip, we went out to breakfast and ventured out to find sprinkles! Let's just say we got a bit lost once we were in the area (GPS was making me go in circles, haha). But we finally found it! It's a cute little shop and we went inside to order. We ended up getting 4 different flavors! We got the Sprinkles, Vanilla Milk Chocolate, Banana and Vegan Red Velvet (the regular one was being restocked). Anyways! We were the only ones in there at that time and after we ordered, we headed back to our hotel. We made a quick video on trying Sprinkles for the first time and overall in my opinion, it was delicious, but to me it's a bit too much frosting and some were really sweet. I really loved the banana one! That one had to be the best for me. Maybe whenever we are near another Sprinkles, we'll try out their other flavors.

Came here after hiking around the park. According to the lady, the ice cream here is made with organic milk. I didn't get a fancy dessert as I was having dinner in 2 hours but I can attest this ice cream is among the best I've had. It's creamy and importantly not colored. (I always check if the mint chip is green or white.) Bonus: they have green tea and an excellent mango habanero for ice cream flavors, and bubble tea!
This place has quite the selection. This visit I chose to get a medium cone, which is two ice cream scoops. I also chose to add fruity pebbles to it and that was plus.

Came to visit! They close super early but we came here around noon for our donuts. First time here and they offered us a $10/ box donut. We filled the entire box up with whatever donuts we wanted, and it was amazing that they still had the poppa tart donut which I wanted to try. I took a giant bite out of it, and it was so yummy! It would've been better if I heated it and the glaze was melty and warm. I recommend heating it up though. Overall, I loved the strawberry pop tart donut even though it was so big I couldn't finish it and only ate a quarter and saved the rest for later! It was delicious and I would definitely eat it again.

Amazing ice cream wonderful customer service!! Love this place the atmosphere is really neat too, right in the art district on grand. Wayward is adjoined to the whole complex and we absolutely love them both!

Yum! So good! I got this recommendation from a blog on pinterest and it was worth it! Its a small little shop with a lot of different ice cream options and a bunch of candy. They make their own marshmallow creme which is mostly why I wanted to go there. Its my favorite ice cream topping. We got the smores sundae to share and it was huge and really good. She put a big scoop of marshmallow creme on it and the torched it. I usually like it more hot and melted like a syrup but this was good too. The service was great. They have a little back patio we sat on and ate our ice cream. Good spot if you are in the area!
Drinks were quickly made and very tastyy, cured my boba cravings l. The shop was cute inside as well :))

There are few Bouchon Bakeries at The Venetian, and this location - the one near the theater was a little hard to find. My family had the macarons, and we had one of each flavor: chocolate, coffee, pistachio, raspberry, salted caramel and vanilla. It was a special buy 5 and get 1 free. Their macarons are huge and the perfect size for sharing, full of great flavor and sweet. My faves were the coffee, salted caramel and raspberry.

Well finally got my long awaited Sprinkles cupcake in. It not often am down on the strip in general but since had visitors in town. Perfect opportunity not only to walk off some Bacchanel Buffet across the street. My friends never seen The Linq so killed two birds with one stone. YAY! As always every time walking down The Linq the exterior sign just screams at me fun! Especially at night with all the bright colors, and cool design. It not only on the outside. Soon as you walk in looking at the display of cupcakes. Bold assortment of different cupcakes. Sooo many had hard time choosing my first Sprinkles cupcake flavor. Talk about throwing curve ball never knew they sold mini cupcakes on top of the healthy side gluten free ones. I love the way all the cupcakes are displayed and every one looks like perfect cupcake (same size, icing nice and smooth even all around, and not one squeezed up next to one another). They do seasonal cupcakes so just cause you seen one this trip might not see it again. But if hit right cycle see it again. Another section that does the ice creams but this trip just looked at cupcakes but next time get something from the other half. I ended up settling on the raspberry cupcake. I really thinking red velvet but wanted something different. Raspberry was awesome! Like mention all the cupcakes look like piece of artwork. I feel guilty that first bite not sure best way attack it. I did both frosting by itself and all. The cupcake by itself amazing really taste hint of raspberry in it. Moist. The frosting was da bomb. Again had nice raspberry flavor not over the top but just right on. The only thing that would say not fan of is the price$$$ But then again for gourmet cupcakes the prices they charge is the going rate. If want indulge in cupcake Sprinkles is great way get the fix in. I know next time walking down The Linq will get my cupcake fix on. The service felt was awesome. I never went was packed. I seen that when gets so busy they make line outside and control amount of people in store at one time. Smart but on hot summer Vegas days not many fans. They have full staff so not much waiting going on. The longest wait is trying to decide which flavor want get cupcake fix on. Talk about nice packaging from the boxes. I just ordered one and simple paper bag nice and Sprinkles sticker seal it. Count I will be back again.

Okay, this place is Phenomenal!!! I had brunch their with my besties (back in November, sue me, I've been lazy) and I have to say this is one of my new favs for Las Vegas!! Our server was super sweet and very knowledgeable about the menu. He started us off with a pastry of our choice and I had a cream puff (Amelia Bedilia would've been proud). Next, I was having a hard time choosing what to eat, so he suggested I chose the corned beef and I'm so glad he did! Let me tell you folks, the French do corned beef WAY BETTER than your granny or your mama!! It was like chunks of jerky-esque beef and delicate diced potatoes. My eggs were fluffy and perfect and the seasoning for this whole dish was absolutely wonderful! I just wish my stomach had been prepared for this meal...it defeated me! Lastly, we headed over to the bakery and picked up some pastries for the road (not like it made it "home") and again, the staff was very cordial and helpful. I will DEFINITELY be back; it's only a question of when!!

My favorite ice cream shop growing up ... I remember ordering the Destroyer, which is some sort of triple banana split mega concoction of deliciousness. I returned here recently, and it was as awesome as ever!

Unique flavors you're never going to realize how much you missed in life until your first bite (lick?) After getting pick-ups since early on in the pandemic from Katrina, the founder, to support her donations to a variety of social justice organizations, we're so excited to be able to continue to do so on a regular basis at this brick and mortar location! Seriously the best ice cream you're going to find - make sure to stock up on some of the take-home pints! We're partial to Song of Fire and Ice (a maple-base ice cream with spicy & crunchy pecans) and the new blueberry flavor was incredible as well. So many gluten-free options (even the waffle cones!) and pup-cups too.

Do not miss an opportunity to eat a donut from The Vegan Doughnut Company. Hands down the best donuts I've ever eaten in my life. You can't go wrong with pretty much any flavor. There is often a long line out the door on weekend mornings, but I promise these donuts are absolutely worth the wait. Can't wait to go back (again) and try more flavors.
Amazing. Delicious. . Lovely service. Great ice cream. We will be back - probably tomorrow. Can't wait!!!! Heavenly. And cute little tables and chairs in air conditioning. Wonderful place.

Terrible line management. Five employees stood in the middle of the store and only was helping customers. Another was sweeping the floor with eight people standing in line. No "Sorry it will be just a moment", no communication whatsoever. Ended up walking out since the customer service was nonexistent.

Welcome to Las Vegas 85C Bakery Cafe, we've been waiting for our Brioche Loaf, Berry Tale, Iced Sea Salt Coffee and all your delicious bread, cakes and pastries for a long time in the greater Las Vegas metropolitan area for years! For those who are not aware what the Hype is about. This particular brand of Bakery has been setting up shop throughout the United States in the past years and have been a huge success because of its price point and delicious items which combines the flavors of Europe and Asia. There is so much to choose from and the shelves are replenish throughout the day. From flavored bread/loaf to pastries like buns filled with berries or mango to ham and cheese croissant. They also sale cake slices and round cakes of various flavors from Tiramisu, Red Velvet, Strawberries and Mango. I've been a fan since visiting their locations throughout the Southern California region for years. How does it work? Upon entering you get a tray and add a paper liner and set of tongs to picked your items that are enclosed in cubicles of plastics stack against the wall and windows. Then you stand in land to get them package with plastic or in a paper box depending your preference. FYI, they have an automatic machine where you can place drink(s) or cake orders for pick up so you don't need to wait in line. Is something I recommend. However, your able to place your drink order when your at the cashier. For the many one star reviews listed, many of the posted reviews deals with the frustrations from the recent soft opening and crazy grand opening weekend. Those folks choose to visit and vent their frustrations which I completely understand but I would advise others that they have been super duper busy these past weeks and according to the staff that I've spoken too, it's been non-stop. So do plan ahead and be patient with the staff. This is the very first location in Las Vegas and the state of Nevada. They have a lot to improve on but honestly they've been doing a good job. FYI: -85C Bakery started in Taiwan and entered the United States market in 2008 with their very first location in Irvine, CA. and it continues to grow with more locations. -Affordable, it's one of the main draw as to why this Bakery have gained a huge following from the public and its common to see customers hoarde or haul like my FamBam, LoL. -It's Known as the, "Starbucks of Taiwan!" 2019 Yelp Review #16

Although it's a big hard to find, its worth the trek through the smoke filled casino. I've tried a variety of macaroons, the chocolate cupcake with marshmallow frosting, and the carrot cake sandwich cookie. All of which were DELICIOUS. I've also had dinner the Bouchon restaurant and they gave us a plate of pastries...a few of which I also saw at the bakery. All I can say is YUM. And I need to start having longer Vegas trips so I can fit in more visits to this bakery. Still so much to try...

We ordered the banana split and the guy prepared it without wearing gloves which I think is unsanitary since its the same person who is collecting the money and preparing the order. This guy who helped us was very nice but the owner should provide gloves for the employees.

Page's is the best. As a dairy lover, I also happen to be lactose intolerant, and so most of my dairy outings are spent wondering if it was worth it. Whenever I hit up Page's, the answer is always, without any hesitation, yes. It was very worth it. Get your soft serve dipped, get it with a freshly warm cookie or brownie, and if you can't decide, get a little bit of everything (really, it's an option). Don't want ice cream? Get a burger! But, actually, get ice cream. Why would you not want ice cream? The line moves fast, the people are awesome, and the ice cream makes it all worth it.
Very disappointed with this place, small selection of ice cream, way overpriced. Some of the ice cream were melted and freeze again, sorbet tasted like water with loads of sugar. Won't be back.

I'm not a huge donut fan, but Donut Bar's funky treats are hard to turn down- their DTLV location and available-til-sold-out hours make an actual visit fairly rare for me, but I've come across their donuts at various events and on appreciation tables at work pretty regularly. I've enjoyed the Salted Caramel, Mexican Hot Chocolate, Blood Orange and Creme Brulee donuts, while the Big Poppa Tart makes a good one to share, huge and stuffed with an actual Pop Tart and likely several days worth of sugar. I tried the Matcha on a recent visit and it was okay, small and not too sweet, but the Strawberry Split has my heart- fresh fruit, whipped cream, photogenic and shareable! Eventually I need to go back for the Caramel Latte donut and their Grilled Cheese. TIP: Go early and check their online menu to be sure they have what you want, selection varies daily.
Best macaroons I have ever had! I always get the pistachio, but this time decided to try the Salted Caramel, OMG my new addiction!!!! I can't wait to get back to Vegas and indulge again!

I get bakery from batch once or twice a week. It's not the best I have ever had but it's good enough. Some of the sweets in particular are a bit bland. The only real flaw though Is the drinks, tea and coffee are both terrible so I end up having to stop somewhere else when out for breakfast. This might be intentional to not compete with the cafes they sell too, not sure.

This one's real easy, top marks all the way around! The macaroons here are easily some of the best I've had, second only to the infamous LadurÃ©e and maybe another bakery I've been to. The usually have about 15 different varieties to choose from and always changing. The cakes here are also impeccable, personal faves are the carrot cake and some of their chocolate variants. Everything is made in house and all in all, one of if not the best bakery in CLT. Check it out!

Saw all the people in line and wanted to try something new. You can customize or get basic flavors. We got chocolate and vanilla on waffle cones with 2 scoops, more than enough! Great bench seating outside to enjoy your dessert . Make sure you park across the far side of the lot or you will get stuck behind the long drive through line!

Good ice cream flavor selections, warm customer service and you can actually see the factory behind the counter. Limited seasonal flavors offered, price reasonable. We had cookies and cream and cookie dough.

Hands down my all-time favorite ice cream spot! I first came into contact with this slice of nirvana in Nashville & was beyond thrilled when the Charlotte location opened. With a number of innovative flavors like Brambleberry Crisp, Goat Cheese & Cherries, Roxbury Road, Milkiest Chocolate, & Whiskey & Pecans, there's definitely something for everyone. Dairy-free options are also available.

I'm no cupcake connoisseur. I enjoy watching Cupcake Wars when it's on, had not a clue this place was owned by someone on the show. It wouldn't have made a difference to me. The line was too long for us to put up with, so we chose to utilize the ATM around the corner. What an adorable idea! We got chocolate marshmallow, red velvet and vanilla chocolate...or something like that. They were all delicious. Thumbs up. Finally a place to rival The Cupcakery! Looking forward to coming back soon.

Went to the Lakewood location after passing by it numerous times. We were waited on almost immediately even though it was busy. The cotton candy tree is magical, & some of the best I've ever had. The strawberry cupcakes took me back to childhood. For everything we bought, I thought it would be more expensive. Truly a pleasureable experience, & great quality candy, popcorn & bakery for what they charge. We will definitely be back, especially after being disappointed by many bakery cupcakes in the past. Highly recommend. :-)

I'm not sure about the fuss. I was in the mood for some gelato or ice-cream and Handel's had 4 stars on Yelp. It's a definite local spot. There's no inside area, so you just order at the window and I ended up eating in the car. I got 2 flavors to try it out, pistachio and Elvis (banana and peanut butter). I always get a nut flavor if they have it. The pistachio didn't have a lot of pistachio flavor even though it had tons of nuts in the ice cream. The Elvis was actually really good, the combo of banana ice cream with peanut butter. It wasn't as awesome as I expected with the great reviews. The serving was huge and the price was cheap, a little over $4 for 2 scoops.

This is one of the best places I've ever been to. Everything here is top notch. The turkey bacon sandwich is heavenly. Add a cup of spicy Tai soup, a lavender lemonade and a chocolate mousse cup to have the best meal in Charlotte.

DELICIOUS!!!! This place is soooo good. You get to pick your ice cream, choose a macaroon flavor and it's then topped with a melted marshmallow!! I got coconut ice cream with an almond macaroon and it was sooooo good. The macaroons are sooooo good!! My brother got cheer swirl ice cream with a strawberry macaroon and he also really liked his. This was my first time here and the owner was also super sweet! I will definitely be returning next time I'm in the area!

I love this place, it's a bit of a drive for me to get there from Tempe, but their butter pecan is worth it! They also have homemade marshmallows- YUM! I've tried a scoop of peanut butter with chocolate covered pretzel pieces, and I've also tried a milkshake with chocolate, peanut butter, and malt, all were just as delicious as the last! The offer pretzel cones which I've been wanting to try! If I ever come here alone I make sure to surprise my boyfriend with their oatmeal cranberry apricot cookies, things are MASSIVE and his favorite!
I wish they had a gluten free cupcake option so I could of tried one but I did really enjoy my shake! And the group I was with were in love with their sprinkle sundaes!!

Savory crepe was delicious. Sweet crepe was overmixed and tough like a quesadilla. Such a shame because the attitude was authentically French but the food was not. I would not recommend waiting 45 minutes like we did.
Yummy yummy yummy! The crack pie ice cream is amazing. Highly recommend. So creamy and rich and they will give you samples of everything.
Yummy matcha ice cream. The red bean pastry was delish also. I wish the cost was a bit lower though.

so reading the reviews for this shop, I was expecting some deliciousness, some extraordinary, some awesomeness and all I got was another "wtf" moment, and a feeling of "should I call and complain and ask for my money back"...I mean, I dropped $25 for 8 donuts...ya let's get to the review... so I found myself in the downtown area recently, and remember hearing about a donut that crunched on top, looked it up and was happy it was there. so I drove over to the spot in downtown, and checked it out. walked into the shop, it's small, narrow, but it gets right to the point. the display of donuts was very nice. they all look delicious, and in my mind I was excited to finally try the assortment I was putting together. I went for 2 of the creme brulee donuts, one that I think had a velvet cake inside, one of the poptart donuts, a white sprinkle, and a chocolate top one and some others. total was $25 (price shock hits, it's donuts!!) but ok I paid it, drove home and dove in with wifey. this is where it just went wrong. now, I usually don't take photos, but recently I have been of the meals and stuff I'm eating or places I'm going to, and this place got the picture... every single donut we ate was dry. they were all over cooked I guess. the batter used had no flavor or sweetness. the flavors were not there, it was like trying to enjoy it but not...I only took a bite or 2 of each donut and trashed it. throughout the day just picked at them all. when I got the one that crunches, the creme brulee one, I was just SO let down. the taste was honestly gross. that mixture of the crunch on the top of your mouth, then mixing it with a soft/dry donut that has no flavor was just really gross. and I'm not picky, especially when it comes to what should have been sweet and delicious, was a major fail. again, every donut was dry, and they all had no flavor or bland flavoring. even the pop tart donut was a bust. the cake mix they use is just no good. I don't know if it was that day or what, but no go for me. now, I've tried pink box donuts which was ok. the only donut shop here in town that seems to be excellent every time is Winchells on Meadows Lane with the subway. that place is 5 star superb. I understand though, this donut bar place, it made it on tv or whatever, and people want to see it, but all these 5 star reviews is just not possible if it's consistently like my experience when quality comes in. check out my photos...you'll see what I mean.

Had to try Novel ice cream after seeing so many good reviews and articles about the shop. The owner, Brandon, does a great job of welcoming customers in, speaking about each flavor, and offering samples. I ended up with German chocolate cake flavored ice cream and loved it. The shop is very small but has outdoor seating to enjoy your treat. Definitely one of the best ice cream shops in Phoenix!

The crack pie has been on my radar since this place opened. My sister was in town recently and was staying at Cosmo, so I met her there and we went to Milk Bar. It's located on the 2nd floor with the other restaurants. This is a walk-up place with no seating, just grab and go! There are places to sit nearby, but it might be nice to add some tables and chairs, especially for those who are eating cake or ice cream. I got the crack pie and she got the cereal milk soft serve. First things first, the piece of pie is tiny! The pies at mickey dees are bigger. I thought for the price of almost $8 it would be a decent size. It was good, but nothing special. It tasted very buttery and the filling was a bit gelatinous, like pecan pie. I am glad I got to try it, but it was nothing special. The cereal milk was very reminiscent of cinnamon toast crunch. Again I am glad I got to try it, but nothing special. I want to try the birthday cake, which they only previously had sold as whole cakes, but now they sell slices. Too bad it's almost $20 a slice. I love cake, but no way I am paying that much ever. Sorry Milk Bar but you are a one and done for me. Pro tip - Target sells Milk Bar baking mixes so you can make these goodies at home. Crack pie, and compost cookies to name a few.
Highly recommended! Best macaron. Vanilla is personal favorite, it is not overwhelming sweet. We came to this place by accident. Now this place has become a must-go for each Vegas trip.
Ice cream was mediocre and I had to ask for the marshmallow which the cookie cup was supposed to come with. Only had 2 flavors of macaroons too which were bland. Tiny two scoops for 8 dollars.

Just as good as the San Diego location! We get a lot of well known eateries from other cities opening in Vegas. Not all of them live up to the hype. Donut Bar definitely does. I came in around 11 am during their soft opening. There was a short line that moved quick. I was getting donuts for a few people so picked a good variety: Caramelized Pineapple, Caramel Latte, Cake Batter, Mud Pie, Red Velvet, Samoa, Chocolate Twix, Blueberry Cheesecake, Banana Caramel and Apple Fritter. Half went to work with Hubby and half came home with me. It is hard to pick a favorite but if pressed I would say the Caramel Latte and Samoa were the faves out of the ones I tried. They post the next days flavors the night before on social media. Check it out before you go so you have an idea of what you want. They are listed in store too but the line moves quick so be ready. Not all of the varieties fit on the counter so don't miss a flavor because you didn't read the list. Don't forget a drink. They have Stumptown Cold Brew, Nitro, Chocolate and Strawberry Milk on tap. See you in line.
Went here to try out their ice cream since they're highly rated. Got half a scoop of the Mackinac fudge ice cream and coconut almond bliss. It was so good! Very rich and creamy

I've watched, and loved, every episode of Cake Boss and I really, REALLY wanted to be blown away by this place... but it just didn't live up to the expectations I had in mind. We got two cream puffs - they were the best thing we ordered and they really were good; a cannoli - the filling had a strange not-quite-smooth/not-quite-gritty texture but a pretty good flavor to it and the shell tasted like it had been deep fried in old grease; a chocolate cupcake with vanilla buttercream frosting - not bad... but not great, either; and a lobster tail (what I was most anticipating after hearing the stories about them on the show) - I'm torn on the lobster tail... the pastry is amazing, super crispy and nicely browned with a nice flavor... but the filling just tastes 'off' - the vanilla has too much of a punch and tastes artificial. I'm sure their ingredients are of great quality but they just didn't work well together today.

Can I put 3.5 stars? The baked goods were decent. We got a whole bunch of biscotti and some miscellaneous breakfast pastries. I would say that the breakfast pastries we got, an apple turnover and some sort of lemon butter crumb pastry were both extremely good. If I was rating this place just on the quality of those two things, i would say 5 stars all the way. We tried another kind of cookie thing with hazelnut on it, and it was just okay for me. The really bad part about this place, the price, gruff service, and to a lesser extent, the confusion of the madness. Walking up, there were two huge lines, so which one do we get in? Nobody had a clue. Turns out, one was the line to order, and one line was to pay. Not a very intuitive process, since the line to pay looked like it was properly roped off as if it were the starting point. Get some signs! Service was relatively quick, but they sure weren't very nice. We were buying stuff for ourselves and stuff for someone else, so we asked for separate boxes. Yea, that didn't seem to go very well with the person taking the order. Annoyed look on her face. Actually, that annoyed look was on all the workers faces. And finally, the price. Wow! At the end of the day, it was probably our fault that we bought too much biscotti, but all in all we spent $50 for a couple pastries, a cookie, and maybe a bag of biscotti that in a normally overpriced environment (if that makes sense) would still only be $20. If I could get the breakfast pastries ($5 each) without waiting in line, I would do it. Unrelated, I am definitely interested in trying the Buddy V's restaurant, also by Carlo.

This isn't just about great ice cream but a great venue as well. The clean, well-lighted, production area behind the glass also reveals the vintage architecture that gives a nod to Cleveland's industrial past. There is plenty of seating on two different levels and the modern decor provides a striking contrast to the building. As for the ice cream, Mitchell's was offering rhubarb the day of my visit. If you are a fan of rhubarb, you can appreciate what I'm saying. Who does rhubarb ice cream!?! It was some of the best ice cream I have ever had! If you're visiting the area, be sure to stop. The hotter the day, the better!

There is something special about this ice cream no lie. Once you walk by the store and smell the fresh waffle cones being made its like light to a fly we were trapped. What they have there is truly a trap that my wife and I were caught in. The staff was very friendly as we tried a few samples and came to the big decision one of everything. The cone is sweet but a hint salty which was mmmmmm I had the honey and vanilla. The only problem I had was it went too fast, and I took my time eating it. Well done as the staff was friendly clean as I noticed the cashier correctly washing his hands after each transaction well done. A++, Jeni we want in to be investors right off the light rail this place is a definite winner in any day after the game or hot day. Plenty of room inside or out time to bring the sweet tooth out.

Best donuts in Cleveland!!!! Their flavors are always amazing and totally worth the drive if you don't live in the area. I live on the East side but have absolutely no issue making the drive because these donuts are incredible. And the sisters that own the place are the sweetest! They are frequently joined by their parents who help out at the shop who are equally nice :) I cannot emphasize enough how amazing this donut shop is. My only complaint is that I wish they were opened 7 days a week so that I could go every day!
Tasty and original flavors, especially spouse like a house and graham central station. Friendly staff and definitely somewhere I will visit again!

This soon not to be hidden gem was a delight. The workers were so helpful and told us about each of the ice cream we sampled. Great nook of a place that will never be a regrettable choice. Their specialty flavors and stuffed treats are a local rarity. Personally, the ice cream waffle sandwich (the Leslie Knope) is my favorite, but the ice cream stuffed donut is a close second.

La flameyyyy!!!! The perfect donut and ice cream proportion. Not too sloppy, and fit perfect in your hands. I got the Cookie Monster mix with the STRAIGHT UP STRAWBERRY and I will be getting that next time I go. The ice cream specialist was so nice and informative. You can tell he loves his job, and is proud to work there. I will be back

I visited Jenis on a Sunday around 4. The line was not too long. I love the look of jenis and it's placement in the design center is great. There's plenty of spots to sit around Jenis. I had the vanilla ice cream as they were out of my first two choices. The vanilla was amazing. Easily the best vanilla ice cream I have ever had! We had no trouble finding on street parking but I would suggest walking, scootering, or ubering there as there are not many spaces available.

As there are not many bakeries in Charlotte (so so sad, compared to my beloved Pittsburgh where there were 6 bakeries on my old street alone), this place already gets a good review from me. But, they also feature many exciting, delicious options, and no cupcakes in sight! Thank god. A cupcake place is not a bakery. This place is faux-French, lots of cute, buttery-goodness inspired by French bakeries but without the price-tag and with more accessibility. The place is also decorated to the nines--it feels a bit like being in Wonderland. Their drink selection is great too! Their number-system could use a little work. I've repeatedly had to get up and remind servers that I'm waiting for food, while they've already moved on to 6 guests after me. Sigh. Be prepared for insane busy-ness at times. And--perhaps--because of that, really shitty baristas and cashiers. They can be very snappy, rude, completely ignore you, and then back talk to you when you try to nicely correct them on a mistake. Hopefully they just need to be retrained on how to deal with a busy environment, and that's not their natural disposition.

I had heard a lot of hype- the birthday cake was overpriced and completely dry. After letting it thaw, it was even worse. I also tried the French toast flavored ice cream. The cashier pointed to the French toast ice cream picture, I paid, and what came out had no toppings on it. That was frustrating, but worse was the taste. It was like salted butter ice cream. I ended up taking 2 bites, and literally throwing it away at the pink counter. You'd be better going to ANY other dessert place around.

I went there today for the first time. I told the one worker that I was new. She seemed annoyed that she had to explain which donut was what. Maybe if they had signs or descriptions, it would help eliminate the annoyance of everyone asking what's that? The donuts were good, but honestly I wasn't blown away. My husband and I tried the glazed, Samoan, maple, PB, lucky charms. They might have been fresh, but I don't think they were. The lucky charm one especially. Just seemed like it was sitting around awhile. The donut dough itself is thick and more like a cake. I was hoping the glazed one would top Krispie Kream but two totally different tastes. They are not light and airy. All in all very good donuts, the concept is cool, just feel like the hype makes it more than what it is

Came here on a Monday, 03/21/22 and there were a couple guests ahead of us in line. The line went by fast. We ordered one Almond Croissant and one Fruit Danish. The texture of both pastries were cooked nicely. It's a messy eat but that's ok. The taste was good and I noticed a hint of lemon which we were not too fond of. I would def like to try other items next time.

Maybe the best ice cream I have had anywhere, ever. NY, Philly, LA, SF, Italy. Anywhere. Vietnamese coffee, chocolate, and toasted coconut. I shared this huge amount of ice cream with my husband. Its probably a good thing we don't live in Phoenix.

When we arrived the line was fairly long, it moved very quickly though and in no time we were picking out our treats. We ended up with a lobster tail, 3 cookies, a canoli, and a mini chocolate ganache cake. All of it tasted wonderful and surprisingly was only about $22. The staff was AMAZING! My oldest son wanted some cherries, and they went in the back and brought several back for him. It made his day lol. Everyone had a smile on their face and made sure we had everything we needed. raeganmirickfoodblog.blo¦

Went there today for the first time and as we were waiting in line we saw one of the workers named shanel, eating with gloves on. Then she started to scratch her face, her arms, and her back and never bothered to change her gloves. Then she started to prep some of the pastries. I ended up buying a cannoli which was really good, but that one employee was just very disgusting. And I have this place 1 star because of her.
Love love love Sprinkles! A "must go" stop for any cupcake lover. They have 2 gluten free options, red velvet and lemon blueberry. Both are AMAZING! Be sure to check out the cupcake ATM!

Why the hype? Took forever to find the bakery in Venentian (under the escalators past the food court on the casino level). Didn't get any of the popular items, but we did like the shredded coconut square and the Better Netter Cookie (with peanut butter cookies and cream). chocolate Roll- bleh.

This is one of the few time where the qoute "the snozzberries taste like snozzberries" were they may not have had snozzberries but I did try the popcorn ice-cream and that is exactly what it tastes like a wonderful buttery, salty, and complete perfection.

Really disappointed. Waited in long line and purchased a nice variety of desserts. All tasted the same - no flavor and very processed/mass produced tasting. Do not recommend this bakery at all. Just a tourist trap.

My wife said, there is a Chi-fil-a in the bottom of the hotel. I shook my head and put on my shoes and after visiting another coffee shop I saw this place was opening. I showed up just in time to be first in line, the police rolled up (because.... well... sometimes the old stereotype is true) and I got to take in the great selection of donuts. The hardest part was was limiting myself. Went back again later in the week to get more donuts (hurray for getting to try more) to share with my wife's employees). Reasonably priced and just plain delicious. Coffee is good too, since what goes better with donuts?
Came here to experience the Christina Tosi enterprise. We had the crack pie, cereal milk ice cream, and a chocolate malt shake. It was all just as delicious as we hoped!

*one of those crazy people who waited in line for 20 minutes during the soft opening at 9:00 p.m. on a Friday night* yes, it's good. yes, it's really good. and really fresh. their dairy free chocolate is incredible. it is so rich and satisfying. I've had bites of Justin's dairy concoctions which have included: lavender, chocolate chip, and salted caramel. from memory, they haven't had mint chocolate chip yet, but I'm sure they will at some point! we've been twice now, but on the third time, when the line was over 20 minutes, we decided to bail. thrilled that CLT is one of the few cities that Jeni's has expanded to. it's such a bright (literally!) spot in South End which makes our neighborhood even better.

Amelie's is a small pastry shop that, according to my good friend that lives in Charlotte, has become incredibly popular since they expanded their hours to 24/7 (whenever that was). As soon as we stepped through the doors tonight, it was apparent. The line to the cash registers extended past the entire glass casing of pastries and almost into the next room. The bakery has an extensive selection of unique and freshly made pastries. There are so many good looking treats to choose from, it makes deciding what to order difficult. Fortunately, the employees are more than willing to help and describe the various sweets they offer. I also noticed on the menu board that they serve breakfast foods, soups, sandwiches, and of course, coffees and teas. I tried their popular salty caramel brownie. It was thick, salty, sweet, sticky, and rich. I could feel the cavities forming in my teeth as I chewed each bite. The design and decor of this place is original and "artsy." There are a lot of handmade decorations, including the chandeliers. The seating is comfortable and cozy and some of the restaurant looks more like a living room than a bakery with couches, coffee tables, lamps, and bookshelves. Almost every seat was taken when we went, even in the atrium in the back. The crowd was very diverse. Live music was going on in one of the rooms.

My head was telling me to go to the gym but my heart said to eat ice cream. Seeing as I'm writing this review, guess which one I listened to. After an extremely satisfying dinner, ice cream was suggested and off we went to Sweet Republic. It was a mad dash to get in before they closed. The staff here is amazing. They didn't rush us out and were extremely courteous as some of us tried multiple samples of all their amazing flavors. I myself only got one sample before instantly falling head-over-heels. It was love-at-first-bite for the Habanero Bacon Avocado. It reminded me a lot of the Vietnamese avocado smoothies and I was happy happy girl. It had that salty-sweet thing that I enjoy immensely with silky ribbons of bacon in it. There was only a slight heat from the habanero that tickles the back of your throat. It was good. It was so so sooo good! It was so good that when Linh L. got me a sample of the Plum & Honey, I ate it without really tasting it and went back to devouring my Habanero Bacon Avocado in a grotesque and savage manner [Thank you, Aileen B., for letting me get another taste out of your ice cream cup. It was ridonkulously amazing with the AZ Queen Bee Honey!]. I also snagged a bite of Yuko H's Basil Lime Sorbet which is her favorite. It was light, fresh, with a strong taste of basil, and really clean in flavor. Linh L's Huckleberry Lemon and Almond-something were also great. The Huckleberry Lemon was extremely flavorful and refreshing. I also got to steal bite after bite of Toffee Banofi --- which apparently is a beloved of Food Network star Alton Brown's! All in all, I'm a fan! I wish they had a location in Chandler but for the sake of my waistline, maybe this is a blessing. ;)
FULL 5 STARS!!!! This place has amazing macaroons with a great variety of flavors, I recommend the strawberry it's so good! If your looking for a bomb desert place THIS IS FOR YOU.

I've been craving macarons for a while and hadn't had any good ones. A relative was going to Vegas for the weekend and I asked him to bring back some macarons from Bouchon Bakery for me, one of each flavor. He said he try. Come Monday morning, he hands me a small bag from Bouchon Bakery. Yay! It was like a rainbow of macarons in a box- topped with a bow. ( Picture: static.px.yelp.com/bphot¦ ) In the box (from left to right) was a rasberry macaron, an orange macaron, a lemon macaron, a hazelnut/cream/(?) macaron, an espresso macaron, and a chocolate macaron. My favorite was the hazelnut/cream/(?) followed by the lemon and the espresso. I found the rasberry too tart and the orange too strong. They were delish AND I did share half of each macaron. 5 stars for delicious snacks and pretty, see-through packaging.

I've had this place bookmarked for quite some time now and I finally made it out there the other day. I put the directions in my GPS and I'm not gonna lie I thought I took a wrong turn because the location in kind of weird. The parking lot is dark but they do have a sign on the outside thats well lit. Anyways, wasn't really sure what to expect and the staff member was super helpful. He let my friend and I sample as many flavors as we wanted and told us kind of the rundown of how things worked. I ended up choosing banana ice cream and cinnamon toast crunch ice cream with a lemon macaroon. It was pretty tasty but I will say the cinnamon toast crunch cereal inside of the ice cream was super... soggy I guess you would say. I didn't care for the texture. The marshmallow was great though! my favorite part. I like the concept, it was reasonably priced, nice staff, clean store and the ice cream definitely cured my sweet tooth. Next time I come I'll try different combo.

I was finally able to try this 'splendid' ice cream during Jeni's ice cream truck tour. Four of us stood in line for 30 minutes and it was worth it to try a free scoop of the Brown Butter Almond Brittle, Brambleberry Cobbler, Gooey Butter Cake and Darkest Chocolate. All were rich and delicious. I will definitely make my way to South End to try the other flavors.

Oh. My.gosh. This place is soo cute, the staff , SUPER friendly. Got there at 8:30 on a Friday. The line was long it moved extremely slow but well worth the wait. Be sure you get s shake, as it has ice cream, the bowls do it. It is made with General Mills cereal that some kids, cannot be found here in the states. Devious twist and offer alternative to milk . I will say there were at least 30 people behind us in line, it took us an hour to get our shakes. We were the last ones that were able to order shakes as they ran out of ice cream. The owner came out and talked with us and gave us a bit of history, as it started in CA as a food truck and has evolved into a franchise. Devious but word to the wise, go early and be patient.
My favorite place to go for ice cream in Pittsburgh! So many different options of flavors and speciality items.
Sweet people with great customer service. The ice cream is delicious! Will definitely come back
Was also promised a gift card for my troubles over 4 weeks ago. Guess what never showed up? Par for the course, I guess.

The donuts here are good; they're dense, unlike a lot of other donut places. You can really tell thy put effort in making them. However, the creme brulee donut was very disappointing. The hype did not match the quality. I think people were just excited about the cracking noise rather than its taste. However, the other donuts were great!

The best tiramisu and gelato in town. Light dinners range from 7-10 dollars. The paninis are fabulous and so are the Cavetelli and meatball. You enter and take a ticket. (If there are people blocking the doorway with deer in the headlight expression yell " excuse me" and then push your way in.) Very clean and laid back atmosphere. Prestis is mostly known as a bakery. Its an after dinner treat in Little Italy. Great sidewalk cafe seating as well as seating indoors. Silverware and cold water are self serve as are the sodas and other beverages. Great place to take a date after dinner. I prefer the Stracciatella ice cream but the spumoni is good too. The lunch specials are hit or miss and I've had one served ice cold. No I'm not kidding. Stick to dessert anx you'll be fine.

You can smell the sweet waffle cones a block away! Jeni's Ice Cream brings a lot of signature items to the table that won't leave you disappointed along with dairy-free options. Furthermore, her waffle cones are made daily, fresh off the griddle. As a consumer, I can appreciate her attention to detail because the flavors and all the elements are equally well thought out and executed. My favorite ice cream is the Gooey Butter Cake. It's made with cream cheese ice cream layered with Vanilla Cake and butterscotch sauce scooped into a waffle cone. Next time you are in the area pay Jeni's Ice Cream a visit, I promise you won't regret it!

It's good! I can't speak to the macaroon thing b/c I don't like macaroons or marshmellows and as a consequence, have not experienced that, but it's a nice little straightforward ice cream shop with some unique flavors. I went here b/c of their malted milk ball, hoping it would match up to the greatest ice cream I ever had at a place which had "vanilla malt ball" and sadly it didn't, but also that was literally my favorite ice cream experience in several decades of life as a person who is not lactose intolerant aka someone had has pretty regularly eaten ice cream. Also I like that their waffle cones aren't too huge b/c the last time I ate a waffle cone it was literally too wide for my small mouth and it cut up the edges of my lips a bit, but not here. Perfectly reasonable waffle cone size.
Got the red velvet, Nutella overload, and the triple chocolate! Definitely recommend going early because donuts sell out fast!

While we wait 4 order others after us r served, I go up and ask, they gave our order to someone else, they say they'll make it right away, they serve others their orders while I'm waiting, another customer order was messed up, they let her leave with free ice cream, I get my order finally, I ask for refund for their screwups and wait, they say if they refund then I have to give ice cream back, I tell them I just witnessed them give someone else free, they say its bc her order was messed up and didn't want to throw it away, I walk away realize 1 of our items is not what was ordered on receipt, go back up, they make the right thing, still wont refund, they kept my receipt. Service is BAD!!!!

Novel Ice Cream is as good as it gets! I wish I had the self control to take a photo, but I inhaled my ice cream stuffed doughnut before doing so! The combination of a warm glazed doughnut with any of their artisan ice cream is almost too delicious to describe with words. YOU NEED TO TRY ONE!!! Brandon and Jenifer are some of the coolest and down to earth small business owner's I've had the pleasure of meeting. Go to Novel, bring your friends, and you won't regret it!

My friends and husband brought me here today. They had all been here before. The friends said we are going for the twice baked almond croissant. And it was amazing. Yes of course I had to get one......and it was the last one. I can't even begin to describe the perfection that I found in this pastry. (My husband had brought me French macaroons from here before. And they were lovely). But my god the almond croissant. I will have dreams about the almond croissant. And that's not all. Rebecca was so amazing helping me find the perfect drink. I said, "caffeine, hot, sweet but not too sweet. " "salted caramel brownie cafÃ© mocha", she says without hesitation. Ok, sounds great. No, great doesn't even begin to describe how perfect this drink was. Milky, smooth, perfection. In the car on the way home (we live an hour away) I told my husband, anytime you want to come here. Just say so and we are on our way. Thank you. Thank you for existing.

I went to the night market about three weeks ago and bought a pint of the edible cookie dough and it was so amazing that I finished it by the end of the weekend! It was so nice and the texture was great. Would DEFINITELY recommend to anybody with a sweet tooth who loves to try new things

AmÃ©lie's is a quirky 24-hour French bakery in the arts district of Charlotte. The place is decorated with mismatched French-themed art and furniture, and the crowd AmÃ©lie's attracts is diverse as well. I was visiting my cousin for the weekend, and we stopped by twice - Saturday night and Sunday afternoon. Saturday night was packed with the line wrapping around to the other room (and I'm told it is usually busy like this during the later hours of the evening). Sunday wasn't as packed but still busy with customers. Saturday night I got the crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e, and on Sunday I bought a coffee and a variety of pastries to take home to Virginia Beach. Next time I come, I hope to try some of their hot sandwiches and get a frozen baguette to bake at home.

Just as amazing as stated. Hot (June at 930pm) night. Smooth, creamy, flavorful ice cream. Service with a smile and really positive attitudes!! (BOTH employees). Chinese food box and cookie were both clever and so useful (see date of experience). My only complaint is that I found this place--I drive by it at least twice a week and now that I know it's there...

Great place to grab a snack and some coffee. The lines appear long at times but really only take about 5 minutes to get through. The day I went they had a special that provided you a free Carlos water bottle with 24.00 purchase. Nice souvenir if you're from out of town.
I go here every week for coffee with friends. It's a fun atmosphere, good pastries, and great service. Love the Park Road location!

I've always wanted to try Jeni's out and I'm so glad I was able to! The flavors that they offer are so unique and artisanal and they had a good amount of choices for dairy free, which is extremely important since 40 million Americans are lactose intolerant! My only complaint is that it's a bit pricey, but if you're going out to eat ice cream at an establishment that makes it fresh in house and has such unique flavors you can't ~really~ complain.

Do you dream in ice cream? If the answer is no, go to Sweet Republic and then go to sleep and you will. Wow. That is really the only way to explain this place. First off it is a very nice inviting little shop that has indoor and outdoor seating and a repertoire of board games (I am up 3 games to 2 on the wife so far at Connect Four). Before we get to the ice cream, let's jump ahead to the toppings. I am very impressed they make everything including the toppings in house. The waffle cone/bowl are just awesome. As for the ice cream, as mentioned it is all very dreamy. Don't worry if you have no idea what you are going to get. The staff including the owners are very patient and nice when comes to tastings. They encourage it! The fan favorite seems to be the salted caramel and it is great. I really love the peanut chip and the cashew turtle is ridiculously good. Your best option is to try 4-5 and then spoil yourself with a 2 scoop or 3 scoop of one of each of your favorites. Another tip is that if you are having these reoccurring dreams of Sweet Republic, don't call your doctor as this is normal. Instead if you can not make it back right away, go to the Whole Foods in Chandler and get your own pint. It is amazing that it tastes the same and fresh from the shop itself. I am amazed that there is not any freezer burn and it has all the creamy happiness as the buying it right there in the store.

Some bakeries are just another inconsequential stop along a railroad of blandness; but Presti's has long been the final destination for top quality Italian pastries and baked goods. This Little Italy gem has been serving fresh baked goodness since 1903 and continues to set the gold standard for quality. Of the countless occasions on which I have patronized this place, never once have I been disappointed. One word of advice however, be mindful of the weekday lunchtime rush as it can get flooded with patrons from UH and other University Circle institutions. From fresh baked bread to cassata cakes, Presti's has a large assortment of authentic Italian specialties and classic baked goods That will surely satisfy even the most selective tastes. Just a few selections include cannollis, tiramisu, cream puffs, custard puffs, creme brule, cookies, cinnamon rolls, croissants, and many others! My personal favorites here are the cassata cake, canollis and the tiramisu, all of which are simply the best in Cleveland. However, you can't go wrong with any of the selections. If you're seeking the best and don't want to settle for less, Presti's takes the cake!

Good carbs, bad carbs, I don't really care. It's located by the clock tower in Venetian and thought it would be perfect to grab a light breakfast from here. They have many delicious pastries and drinks to choose from. The line was long at first but went by quickly with how fast the employees were attending to everyone's order. The best part of service is also keeping in mind about time and not making customers wait too long which I found to be a great at Bouchon bakery because they were fast. My husband and I both ordered iced coffee which was good both times we came here. Tasted like regular iced coffee and had milk, cream, sugar on the side for you to add your own preferred amount. As for the pastries, we ordered the strawberry danish, chocolate almond croissant, almond croissant and fachiche. Seriously all of these pastries were so good that with every bite I didn't know if I should feel guilty or happy. The almond croissant and strawberry danish were my top favorites. I've never tried strawberry danish and now it's one of my favorites thanks to Bouchon. My husband loved the almond croissant and barely shared with me which shows how delicious it was. This bakery is convenient, delicious, and not too pricey so do check this place out.

Employees were really nice and plenty of staff readily available to help. There was plenty of options and definitely really good cupcakes. I ordered a red velvet sundae and came back to try the cupcake ATM and ordered a black and white cupcake. Perfect spot for late night sweets on the strip.

I love this place. I have been coming for 8 years now. I wish they still had the sandwiches they use to serve but beggars can't be choosers. One of my favorite places to go and grab a coffee late night

So far it was delicious worth the wait!!! Make sure to grab a number as soon as you get there, you might have to wait about 30 min to an 1 hour. The bakery has good delicious deserts. The strawberry cheesecake is super smooth with a bread crust with a huge sweet strawberry on top, the cannoli has a nice crunch and sweet shell with a delicious cream, you might also want to try their red velvet cupcake too you can taste the delicious cream cheese icing with a red chocolate moist bread. The only down side about this bakery is the wait to be honest but its expected since it is new and of course Cake Boss is famous for his deserts and who wouldn't want to try a piece of this now that they are in the west coast! Hope you all enjoy and have the patience to wait for your sweets!

Still a good donut/doughnut! I stopped in recently at their new brick and mortar storefront in Lakewood. I went with the strawberry sprinkles, lemon lavender, and the maple with coconut bacon.
